description: MUST-FAIL: textual equality trap. Two distinct artifact types produce the same 64-char hex digest by coincidence because their canonical forms are identical. A verifier MUST NOT treat equal hex strings as a match; it MUST recompute from the cited bytes under the declared type context. Bare hexadecimal equality alone is not a join.
spec_ref: draft-mih-sokolov-scitt-payload-binding-00 §6.1 ('The two values actually being compared must share an established comparison context. Bare hexadecimal equality alone is not a join. Equal-looking hex values computed under incompatible digest contexts are coincidental, not equivalent.')

registry_entry.digest_context: jcs-n; exclusion set {b_id, weight}; 64-char lowercase hex

erroneous_verification.mistake: Verifier has artifact-B bytes in hand, observes artifact-B derived_id equals the carried digest, and concludes the reference is verified.
erroneous_verification.why_wrong: The reference declared type 'artifact-a'. The verifier MUST recompute from the cited artifact using the digest context registered for 'artifact-a'. Artifact-B bytes under 'artifact-b' context coincidentally yield the same digest — that coincidence is not a join.

correct_verification.step_1: Resolve type 'artifact-a' from registry to get its digest context
correct_verification.note: If the verifier only possesses artifact-B bytes, it cannot verify this reference; the comparison context cannot be established.
